subject: botany_2
question_text: Explain in brief how plants absorb essential elements.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.52, printed question 166. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Printed under STAR QUESTIONS PLUS (p.52), not in an SAQ chapter, but Guess Paper 4 sets it as a Section B question and cites P 52(166) — so it is authored at 4 marks. Examiner audit revision (2026-09-05): the insider note no longer states a share of the marks, and the symplast step no longer claims that spending energy is what makes that phase slow (NCERT states only that uptake into the symplast is slow and active).

insider_note: Passive against active is the whole answer. Name both phases and say which one needs energy: the apoplast phase is passive, the symplast phase is active.

steps.label: The two phases
steps.margin_note: Name both phases before explaining either.
lines: Absorption of essential elements happens in TWO
phases:
a) the apoplast phase
b) the symplast phase
steps.why: The two phases differ in whether a membrane is crossed, and that single difference decides everything else in the answer — speed, direction and energy cost.
common_mistakes: Naming one phase only. The question needs both.
Calling them 'active and passive' without the names. Apoplast and symplast are the terms.
steps.memory_tip: Outside the cells, then inside them: apoplast then symplast.

steps.label: Apoplast: the passive phase
steps.margin_note: Speed, direction relative to the gradient, and the word passive.
lines: a) APOPLAST:
Ions are taken up rapidly into the outer space
or free space of the cells.
The movement is ALONG the concentration
gradient.
No membrane is crossed and no energy is used.
So it is a PASSIVE process.
steps.why: Moving down a gradient releases energy rather than costing it, which is why nothing has to be spent for the apoplast phase.
common_mistakes: Calling the apoplast phase active. It is PASSIVE.
Saying ions cross membranes here. They do not; that is the symplast.
steps.memory_tip: Downhill and outside the cells: nothing to pay.

steps.label: Symplast: the active phase
steps.margin_note: Mirror the apoplast lines point for point: speed, direction, energy, name.
lines: b) SYMPLAST:
Ions are taken SLOWLY into the inner space of
the cells.
The movement is AGAINST the concentration
gradient.
It requires metabolic energy.
So it is an ACTIVE process.
steps.why: Entry into the symplast means crossing the plasma membrane, so this phase needs metabolic energy and the uptake is slow.
common_mistakes: Saying the symplast phase is faster. Ions are taken in SLOWLY in this phase.
Leaving out 'metabolic energy'. It is what makes the process active.
steps.memory_tip: Uphill and inside the cells: it has to be paid for.

steps.label: Flux, influx and efflux
steps.margin_note: Three short definitions. Do not skip this mark; it is the cheapest one here.

lines.text: Flux in = influx; flux out = efflux

lines: The movement of ions is called FLUX.
Inward movement into the cells is INFLUX.
Outward movement out of the cells is EFFLUX.
steps.why: These three words are the vocabulary the rest of the chapter uses, so the question is partly a check that the terms are known.
common_mistakes: Swapping influx and efflux. IN is influx; OUT is efflux.
Leaving the three terms out. They are a whole mark and take three lines.
